body:
17 Nov 2026, P2-25 SLICE 4 (the rehome) BUILT, PR #118 (ready; built, not walked; NOT deployed; the item stays todo). Slice 4 is the release gate of slice 3 and is satisfied only when #118 is merged (the :main image carries slice 3 without it until then).
WHAT: rehome.py in the hourly library link (scanner.link_library) judges the LIBRARY files of worklist refs by their tags (after each page's own link transaction, 100 songs per write transaction) and re-points song_file rows that belong to another song (id, added_at, meta, source kept). It never touches a file on disk and never a like, entry, play or saved queue (tests that fail if one moves; a runtime guard that raises on any write under a real folder). The worklist is emptied only by a COMPLETE pass; refmerge.repair then runs in the same link. repair_copy.py = the slice 3 copy discipline written once (before-rehome, own settings; its text says the check is the header only, not an integrity check). rekey_audit.py + audit_stack.py check rekey [--db COPY --python 3.12] (read-only, exit 0/1/2). tests/test_stopgap_expiry.py: markers say 'remove after 0.1.0' and the suite fails when the server version is past it (assumes the first release is cut as 0.1.0). Phone: encore_split_test.dart on two REAL responses the server test saves; no app code changed.
CHANGES YOU MAY OVERRULE: (1) KEEP RULE: a file stays when its ref is one of the refs of the FIRST TIER of evidence (refs.matches; find is its first row), not only when find returns it: duplicates keep their files, an ISRC still beats a name. (2) the rehome runs AFTER each page's link transaction. (3) refmerge.repair now also runs with live threads. (4) A file nobody can judge (no readable tags, or the placeholder artist with no id) stays AND its ref stays on the worklist (rule 6), REVERSING the first draft of this branch. Reason found in the history: the old find matched the placeholder by name until 14 Nov 2026 (#78), so older databases may hold nameless files glued together. Cost: rekey_audit FAIL by design and N-36 blocked on that Host until the file is tagged or removed; said in docs/18, the design, CHANGELOG and RELEASE-CANDIDATE 4b.
PROOF: tests first for the rehome (31 of 34 red on a stub); audit tool, guard and copy helper proved by mutation. Merged tree on Python 3.12.13: server suite 2589 passed, 13 skipped, 1 xfailed; app suite 3305 passed; ruff, format, mypy, check_rows, check_order, analyze, dart format clean. 36 mutations of the rules red, 1 green and equivalent (rehome before the link transaction; the stale-holder hazard is red). On a COPY of VM 108's DB (original sha256 unchanged): 40 keys rewritten, worklist 0 (as your dry run); audit_stack check rekey on the repaired copy = PASS; worst case, all 12 library refs force-listed: 12 kept, 0 moved, every table identical. audit_people.py scripts 12 PASS; audit_probes.py scripts PASS.
NOT DONE (P2-25 stays todo): the phone's normalizeForMatch/CoverFallbacks.key on the Dart fold (B-46) is a follow-up the design names that has NO board owner (P2-12 slice 8 removes the phone's name matching; building it may be wasted work: your call, and until then P2-25 is not marked); audit_stack check library on a real stack (Docker); the walk. The rehome has only run on SYNTHETIC data (the real worklist is 0): read it on each real database before the release with check rekey.
LIMITS: (a) the phone's audio key has no file id: a split that gives the old song a file with the same size, suffix and bitrate leaves its download as is; (b) the album test proves the song list the album page reads (watchAlbumTracks), not the album's own row; (c) the length is compared within 3 s: a ref whose duration was filled after its file was attached can split a correct pair (a duplicate, the safe direction).
